topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: A worker has not answered for two seconds. It might have crashed, the network might be delayed, its reply might have been lost, or the client might be paused. These possibilities look similar from one observation but imply different recovery actions. Distributed architecture becomes difficult when a component must act without knowing which explanation is true.

topics.title: 10.1.1 Distinguishing Crash, Omission, Delay, and Corruption
topics.summary: A crash-stop model assumes a participant stops taking steps and does not resume. A crash-recovery model permits a participant to restart, often retaining durable state but losing memory. An omission means an expected message is not delivered or processed. A delay means it arrives later than expected. Corruption or Byzantine behavior is a different and stronger problem: a participant or communication path can supply incorrect information, perhaps inconsistently to different peers.

blocks.text: These categories are assumptions for reasoning, not labels an observer can always assign accurately. A TCP disconnect establishes a connection event, not the precise state of a business transaction. A process that restarts at the same address can retain its database while losing its connection state and counters. A process can also be alive but unable to make progress because its disk is full.

blocks.text: Specify which failures the implementation is intended to tolerate. The companion tests process restart, interrupted transactions, dropped application replies, unavailable dependencies, malformed frames, and bounded overload. They do not implement Byzantine consensus or verify the behavior of a failing storage controller. Cryptographic transport protection, replicated storage, and operational recovery would add different guarantees, not magically extend every test already performed.

topics.title: 10.1.2 Treating Failure Detection as a Decision Under Uncertainty
topics.summary: A timeout is a policy for how long to wait, not proof of remote death. Its practical value is that it bounds local resource commitment and triggers a defined next action. That action may be to return an uncertain result, retry with the same identity, query status, or move responsibility to a durable recovery workflow.

topics.title: 10.2.1 Separating Wall Time from Elapsed-Time Budgets
topics.summary: Wall time answers questions such as when a log entry occurred relative to a calendar. An elapsed-time clock answers how much time has passed within a process or machine clock domain. Use std::chrono::steady_clock for the companion’s local deadlines, because their purpose is to bound elapsed waiting rather than to match a civil timestamp.

blocks.text: Do not serialize a steady_clock::time_point and assume another host can interpret it. Its epoch and relationship to another process’s clock are not a cross-machine protocol. An RPC can convey a remaining duration, with the receiver applying its own budget rules, or a wall-clock deadline under an explicitly managed synchronization and uncertainty model. Neither choice removes network transit time automatically.

blocks.text: A practical budget calculation starts at admission. A 500 ms request that spends 350 ms waiting has only 150 ms left for connection establishment, execution, and response. Resetting a fresh 500 ms timeout at each stage silently expands the end-to-end allowance. A deadline carried through local stages is easier to audit than unrelated per-call durations.

blocks.text: Wall-clock timestamps remain useful for operators, but comparisons across hosts have uncertainty. Record timezone offsets, preserve source identity, and avoid using a one-millisecond ordering difference as proof of causality when clock synchronization error could be larger. A log aggregation system can sort records without proving that this is their true causal order.

topics.title: 10.2.2 Defining Expiration and Restart Behavior
topics.summary: Expiration needs a boundary convention. In this companion, now >= end means an elapsed-time budget is expired. A cache entry is not usable at exactly its expiration tick. Tests at equality are valuable because off-by-one assumptions often differ between callers and implementations.

blocks.text: Persisted deadlines require special care. A local monotonic timestamp stored before a reboot may not retain meaning after restart. Persist a business expiration in a supported time representation, or persist enough state to reestablish a policy on recovery. A job’s durable acceptance and its caller’s interactive waiting budget are different concepts: the client can stop waiting while the accepted job remains pending.

blocks.text: HarborDispatch deliberately keeps background delivery alive after the submitting RPC ends. That is an application decision, not a universal recommendation. A payment authorization, a cache refresh, and a batch report may need different expiration behavior. Each requires a definition of whether an expired job is cancelled, retained for inspection, or still completed.

Saturation is not appropriate for every counter; logical clocks in this chapter instead reject overflow rather than silently changing their ordering meaning.

reading.title: Review and solution reasoning
paragraphs: A logical clock preserves a direction of implication: causal precedence implies increasing logical time. An unrelated pair can also have increasing values. A correct explanation therefore names the communication edges instead of treating every numeric comparison as causality.
